PASS applies only to the newly limited theorem A–G together with the complete concrete dependency H. original_S15_completed=false; general_fixed_background_measure_classification_unresolved=true. The historical original-task INCONCLUSIVE report and the preserved fresh cold candidate=false remain unchanged. Their verdicts, hashes and reading flags were not used as mathematical premises.

A and F check. In an affine chart, G(z,y)=log|z−y|²−log(1+|z|²)−log(1+|y|²)+1. The stipulated operator therefore gives δ_y−κ_FS. Rotation invariance and the uniform distribution of d_chord(x,0)² under κ_FS give mean zero. The bounded kernels max(G,−L) decrease to the actual integral Q, and their uniform volume-L¹ bound prevents an identically minus-infinite limit. This establishes the canonical representative, its genuine pole values and its full current κ_FS+dd^cQ=μ. Under the continuous-potential hypothesis, the uniform logarithmic bound and localized Riesz decomposition prove non-polarity; the cold note's capacity proof is also valid. Curve slicing and two applications of Fubini prove product non-pluripolarity.

The bounded corrected-product expansion has precisely one surviving curve factor, giving N h₀^m⊗(κ_FS+dd^cp). Restriction to {p>−j} before increasing the truncation level proves the unbounded pullback formula directly. For nonpolar μ, the pole part of Q has μ-mass zero, so the actual product is cν and its finite mass is NV₀. Conversely, a separated solution has both full curve-current mass and non-pluripolar mass equal to one. Its positive polar remainder vanishes, and harmonic distributional uniqueness gives p=Q+C canonically everywhere. This proves F's normalized uniqueness and its boundedness and continuity equivalences, without adding exponential existence or stretching assertions for arbitrary unbounded Q. Pullbacks of the factor's bounded mass-collapse sequence prove v_−(H)=0. Closedness of h₀ would force constant bounded mass by Stokes, contradicting v_−(h₀)=0; restriction to a factor section then proves H is nonclosed.

B's variational proof is valid. Rotation smoothing gives finite Dirichlet energy for Q. Testing the distributional identity with regularized absolute values produces the continuous H¹→L¹(μ) trace. Central SU(2) smoothing induces radial averages on the curve; local submean inequalities and upper semicontinuity identify their pointwise limit with the canonical representative, including at poles. Strong H¹ convergence then identifies the trace μ-almost everywhere. Smooth approximation and regularized positive parts justify the subsequent Sobolev tests and preserve the trace under positive-part operations.

J_λ is proper, coercive, strictly convex and strongly lower semicontinuous. Its convex epigraph is weakly closed, so Hilbert compactness supplies the minimizer. Bounded smooth variations yield the stated Euler current, with the constant determined by the unit total mass. The canonical Green representation gives q_λ≤1, hence a bounded density relative to μ. The kernel bound gives a finite lower bound, and Dini's uniform kernel-tail estimate gives continuity. The additive shift produces exactly the scalar-one curve equation. The energy identity for two bounded solutions proves uniqueness.

The independently supplied compact-homotopy proof also checks. Uniform kernel tails make the Green operator compact on bounded μ-densities. The normalized maps T_t are continuous and collectively compact, including at t=0 by uniform Taylor expansion. Their fixed points are exactly the normalized curve solutions. The barriers bound every fixed point by osc(Q), so the ball of radius osc(Q)+1 has no boundary fixed point. The constant endpoint has degree one; the primary Leray–Schauder result therefore supplies a fixed point for every specified λ>0. No smooth-volume density theorem is used.

C and D retain the correct constants. U_λ=log(c)/λ+w_λ has the scalar-one product equation and supremum log(c)/λ+sup w_λ. Subtracting that supremum changes the coefficient to c exp(λ sup w_λ). Every constructed bounded potential satisfies the actual all-scale stretching definition using the genuine constant t inf p, and satisfies p≼0. The energy barriers give Q−sup Q≤w_λ≤Q−inf Q for every λ>0. Consequently exp(λw_λ)=1+O(λ) uniformly; Green inversion and the exponential normalization give the whole-family O(λ) convergence claimed in D. Supremum normalization preserves the rate. A genuine critical curve subsolution dominating μ must have full current μ by the same mass-one argument, hence is Q+C. The mean constraint and supremum constraint give precisely the stated separated order characterization.

E checks. Layer cake gives the uniform truncated-kernel error at most (2C/δ)exp(−δL/2) under the power ball-growth hypothesis. Thus the actual potential is finite and continuous. The weighted unit-circle probability has the required growth bound with δ=1 and C=2(1+ε). Direct Fourier integration gives Q(e^{iφ})=1−log 4−ε cos φ on its support, so its potential is nonconstant there. The circle and its product with X₀ have zero smooth ambient volume, establishing a substantive singular example.

G checks over the entire genuine competitor class. The bounded BGL comparison application has a smooth constant barrier ρ≤0 below both inputs, strict background H, bounded difference and strict ratio exp(−λε)<1. Its section expressly removes BMP, and the comparison hypothesis is an inequality of actual measures. The cold modified-comparison reconstruction is independently valid as well: H satisfies the torsion bounds; sufficiently small τ and s place the nonempty comparison set inside {p<r} and make its comparison factor times (1−τ)^N exceed the assumed ratio. The positive τ^N H^N term then forces that set to have zero smooth volume. Canonical submean recovery and upper semicontinuity show that a nonempty strict comparison set has positive volume, giving the contradiction. This does not assert a uniform positive lower mass.

For an arbitrary exponential subsolution r, choose p=U_λ−M and a truncation level with −j<inf p. The equality-set maximum inequality applies only to bounded r_j, p and max(r_j,p). Its first branch lies inside {r>−j}, where finite-level locality recovers the competitor's extended measure; its other branch uses the floor's actual measure. Thus max(r,p) is a bounded exponential subsolution and lies below U_λ. This proves greatestness even for competitors with extra poles or excess or infinite mass, while preserving canonical pointwise order. Bounded uniqueness follows in both directions. Shifting any scaled subsolution by log(a)/λ−sup v makes it an exponential subsolution. Evaluating the resulting order at one fixed finite point and letting λ decrease to zero proves a≤c. The explicitly computed bounded finite equation attains c in all three specified classes. No unbounded exponential uniqueness or nonseparated critical uniqueness follows or is claimed.

H checks in full. The free action and the t-shift by 4π prove proper discontinuity; the explicit C* bundle charts descend to elliptic bundle charts. The compact sphere-and-strip parametrization proves compactness and connectedness. Writing F=β−α and ρ=dt∧d^ct gives dω=−dt∧F≠0, d(ω²)=0, and ω³=6αβρ. The fibre integral of ρ is 4π, so the actual volume is 24π and ω²/(24π) supplies the normalized closed positive test.

For I, B_δ is globally smooth after extension by zero and has a finite pairing bound against every normalized test. If C_δ had a bounded subsequence, Lamari would produce genuine normalized quasi-psh potentials dominating a fixed multiple of B_δ. The supplied submean propagation establishes global L¹ compactness. The limiting concentration dominates the local divisor. Siu is applied only to positive CLOSED local corrections; their smooth differences have zero geometric Lelong contribution, so the analytic upperlevel sets patch globally. The connected lifted divisor forces every translate w₀=q^m z₀ into that analytic set. The power-series argument at [0:1:0:1] forces all local defining functions to vanish, contradicting its dimension bound. This proves divergence against the entire test family.

For II, the chosen matrix parameters remain in a compact subset of GL₂. The actual compact curves are embedded, and their incidence map is a submersion also at infinity and at w₀=0. Compactly supported fibre integration therefore gives globally smooth semipositive CLOSED forms. Compactness of the parameter family gives uniform ω-degree. The stated parameter change, Jacobian and tangent vector yield the printed local coefficient matrix and fixed-δ C∞ convergence. The explicit bump is smooth across its boundary, normalizes correctly, and has central minimum Z⁻¹exp(−16/15). Together with k_* and the symmetric slope moments, this gives the required horizontal bound with a strictly positive constant independent of δ.

For III, the global translation average preserves strict positivity and dd^c-closedness and has uniformly bounded degree. Its vertical coefficient has the stated concentration lower bound throughout V_δ. In the specified tangent convention, Q_{η²}=2det(H)H⁻¹, so H=√(det Q/2)Q⁻¹ is the unique positive root and η³=(3/√2)√(det Q) times the coordinate volume. Uniqueness makes the roots patch globally. The determinant bound and volume μ(V_δ)=δ²/4096 give root-volume growth proportional to √A_j. Fixed-δ smooth convergence suffices to select each actual ε_j; no uniform-in-δ convergence or global limit T_{δ,0} is needed.

For IV, the resulting Γ_j are actual smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed global forms of bounded degree and divergent root volume. Tosatti–Weinkove applies separately to every fixed smooth positive Hermitian h and every smooth positive volume η_j³; multiplying its potential by 2π matches the task operator. Stokes gives ∫(h+dd^cu_j)∧Γ_j=∫h∧Γ_j. Pointwise matrix AM–GM then gives c_jV_j≤(∫h∧Γ_j)³/V_j²→0. The potentials are smooth, supremum-normalized and strictly h-psh. This proves mass collapse for EVERY h, rather than only a selected metric or test family. For h₀=ω the product is a fourfold and c=96π/M.

The old n5 metric counterexample is correct: for κ=κ_FS+dd^cφ, the unchanged kernel produces μ+dd^cφ instead of μ; taking μ=κ_FS already disproves the old exact construction. The new explicit FS hypothesis removes that defect. The historical missing central-density qualification is supplied by the explicit bump and verified calculation. These are substantive changes in the new limited submission, not retroactive corrections to the old verdicts. The cold note's conditional final mass-collapse implication was insufficient without Γ_j; the present complete I–III proofs establish its antecedent independently.

Harmless wording and citation clarifications: BT's recursive definition is equation (2.1), its decreasing-continuity statement is Theorem 2.1, and multilinearity is Corollary 2.2; the current article corrects the older citation. Choosing the comparison barrier also ≤0 matches BGL's section conventions. The radial rotation-kernel sentence is made precise by choosing central SU(2) kernels. None requires a new mathematical argument. No conclusion from the inaccessible companion manuscript, numerical diagnostics, prior PASS assertions or workflow metadata is needed.

passages.statement: For locally bounded psh functions v₁,…,vₖ on a domain in ℂⁿ, k≤n, recursively defined Bedford–Taylor products are positive closed, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing convergence to locally bounded psh limits. [Bedford–Taylor, equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).

These bounded constructions require no BMP. [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, §2.1 and Proposition 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1).

Psh functions on bounded domains are quasicontinuous for this capacity. [Bedford–Taylor, Theorems 3.5 and 6.9](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).
